Work History

Until The Ink Runs Out

Role
Art Direction
Organization
Eighteen Visions
Platforms
Vinyl LP

Until the Ink Runs Out is a personal record-artwork project built around color, texture, and oversized typography.

The cover brings an abstract painted surface and a sharply composed title into one physical object: an image designed to be held, seen, and lived with.

A cover with a physical presence

The artwork starts with an intentionally tactile field of color. Its surface stays loose and atmospheric while the title brings structure, scale, and a strong visual rhythm to the sleeve.

The resulting cover is less about decoration than tension: soft marks behind hard-edged type, and an intimate object presented at a deliberately oversized scale.

From image to object

Photographing the record upright turns the cover into part of the work. The room, the shadow, and the slight shift in perspective make the design feel present rather than merely displayed.

That translation from flat artwork to physical presence is the point of the project: the image becomes an artifact with weight, scale, and a place in the world.

A personal practice

This is an ongoing space for experimenting with image, type, and the ways a designed object can carry a feeling.

Until the Ink Runs Out keeps that exploration close to the things that make personal work rewarding: making something physical, looking at it closely, and letting the details stay visible.
